To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
celecoxib does not prevent fibrosis in the BDL rat model, and that celecoxib is not a cox-2 inhibitor in the liver.

1. Celecoxib does not prevent fibrosis in a rat model of chronic liver injury and fibrogenesis; 2. Celecoxib treatment does not alter hepatic COX-2 expression or prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) production; and 3. Celecoxib reduces hepatic inflammation and liver injury.

(i) celecoxib did suppress cox 2 levels in the kidney but not in the liver, (ii) celecoxib had no effect on fibrosis, (iii) there was no change in the expression of TGF-β1 and αSMA, (iv) celecoxib reduced liver injury as indicated by reduced serum AST and ALT levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cyclooxygenases (cox) 1 and 2 in hepatic fibrogenesis.
the use of selective COX-2 inhibitors for the prevention of liver fibrosis.
the role of cox 1 and cox 2 and their respective products in the development of liver injury and the subsequent development of liver fibrosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
celecoxib does not inhibit cox 2 and does not prevent liver fibrosis.
celecoxib did inhibit cox 2 and its downstream products in kidney but not in the liver.
celecoxib at a dose of 10 mg/kg/day does not prevent fibrosis in a model of liver injury and that the effect of celecoxb at a higher dose remains to be seen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
celecoxib, at the dose used, was not effective in inhibiting the cox-2 pathway in the liver of the rats with BDL and that this may have contributed to the lack of effect on fibrosis.
the use of cox 1-selective inhibitors in liver fibrosis is not supported by current data and cox 2-selective inhibitors have not been shown to be effective in preventing fibrosis in the BDL model.
the use of cox 1 selective NSAIDs in the setting of chronic liver injury is unlikely to be of benefit, and may even be harmful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cox 2 is not a key mediator of fibrogenesis and cox 2 blockade does not prevent fibrosis in the BDL model of rat hepatoxicity.
celecoxib is not effective in preventing fibrosis in bile-duct ligated rats.
the use of a cox 2 inhibitor in this model of liver injury and subsequent fibrosis does not alter the extent or progression of fibrosis (2).
